rq_cta_text: Want a personal verdict on your Bitcoin plan?
rs1_p: A fixed amount every week or month (DCA) instead of guessing the right day. The DCA calculator shows what fees take from a monthly plan.
rs2_p: Savings you won't touch for years can sit on a hardware wallet you control, with the recovery phrase written down offline. Compare hardware wallets.

q_best: What is the best Bitcoin retirement calculator?
a_best: One that shows its assumptions. Look for a calculator that lets you set your own spending, retirement age, life expectancy, growth and inflation, works in your currency, shows the result year by year and says the scenarios are not forecasts. This one does that in euros, runs in your browser, stores nothing and needs no sign-up. It leaves out tax and market falls, so read the result as a range.
q_eu: Can I retire on Bitcoin in Europe?
a_eu: Yes, but the tax on selling depends on where you live. Germany exempts Bitcoin held for more than a year and Czechia after three years, while Slovakia taxes every sale as income and adds health insurance contributions. In the EU, the provider you buy from should hold a MiCA licence, which you can check on the ESMA register. Keep a record of every purchase for your tax return.
q_bear: What happens to a Bitcoin retirement in a bear market?
a_bear: You sell more Bitcoin for the same spending, so the stack can run out early. Bitcoin has fallen 70% or more from a high four times since 2011 ({falls_years}, US dollar month-end prices). This calculator assumes steady growth with no falls. If the price never rose at all, spending {s30} a year from {age} to {life} would need about {flat30} today. A cash reserve lets you avoid selling after a fall.
